note: Dimension = number of elements in a basis. Both define the same object; Apostol adds dim{O}=0, Strang adds dim R^n=n as examples. Well-definedness is a separate theorem (a212/s209), not part of this definition, so the definitions themselves are the same object. Strang's def is genuinely general (matrix/function spaces in s204), not R^n-only, so strict-same rather than special-case.

Basis = (finite) set/sequence that is independent and spans. Apostol names it 'finite basis' because his framework allows infinite-dim spaces, but the notion here is a finite independent spanning set; Strang's basis is also a finite sequence. Neither treats infinite bases in this block, so scopes coincide -> strict-same.

Unique representation relative to a basis. a211 proves uniqueness of the coefficient n-tuple via independence; s208 states existence (spanning) plus uniqueness (independence). Same theorem; existence is definitional from spanning, so the load-bearing content (uniqueness) matches.

Invariance of basis size: all bases of a space have the same number of elements. Both are general finite-dim results; only the proofs differ (Apostol via exchange lemma 15.5 used twice; Strang via W=VA / nonzero nullspace). Different proofs, same theorem -> strict-same.

a203 (Thm 15.5) is the general exchange lemma: k+1 elements in the span of k independent elements are dependent. s205 is the R^m instance ('more vectors than rows -> dependent'; 7 vectors in R^5 dependent), proved by counting free variables of Ax=0. Proper R^n restriction of the abstract lemma.

Definition of linear dependence. a205 applies to an arbitrary (possibly infinite) set S via 'some finite subset has a nontrivial vanishing combination'. s203 is a finite sequence (with the 'one vector is a combination of the others' rephrasing). Same core notion; Apostol's is the proper generalization to infinite sets -> special-case.

a206 (Thm 15.7b): any n independent elements in an n-dim space form a basis (plus 15.7a extension to a basis). s200 is the R^n matrix packaging: n vectors are a basis for R^n iff their columns form an invertible matrix (independence = Ax=0 only x=0, spanning = Ax=b solvable). Overlap on 'n independent R^n vectors form a basis'; s200 adds the invertibility characterization and drops the extension part, so a loose R^n special-case.

HARD CASE (independence: negation vs positive). a213 defines independent = not dependent and stresses 'not restricted to finite sets'; s201 gives the positive definition for a finite sequence in any vector space. The negation-vs-positive difference is presentation only and identical on finite collections. The deciding factor is scope: Apostol covers possibly-infinite sets, Strang only finite sequences -> proper restriction -> special-case, not strict-same.
s202 is linear independence specialized to matrix columns in R^n (only solution of Ax=0 is x=0; nullspace = {0}). Concrete R^n/matrix restriction of the general independence notion a213.

Definition of 'finite dimensional' (has a finite basis, or is {O}). Strang never formally defines finite-dimensional in this block; closest touch is s204's remark that dimension applies to abstract spaces, but no matching object.
Pure notation object n = dim V. Strang emits no standalone notation object for dimension (the concept lives in s210).
Example: if O in S then S is dependent. No Strang counterpart in this block.
Ordered basis as an n-tuple (e_1,...,e_n). Strang does not introduce ordered bases / coordinate ordering in this block.
Example: a superset of a dependent set is dependent (equivalently every subset of an independent set is independent). No Strang counterpart here.
Definition of components/coordinates of x relative to an ordered basis. Strang does not define coordinate components in this block (s208 gives uniqueness but not the named coordinate tuple).
Infinite-dimensional spaces (space of all polynomials). Strang stays finite-dimensional throughout this block; s204's function-space example is finite-dim (dim 2). No counterpart.
Example: distinct-exponent exponential functions e^{a_k x} are independent (analytic proof by induction). Abstract function-space independence example with no Strang counterpart.

Meta-remark plus examples that independence/basis/dimension extend beyond column vectors (2x2 matrices dim 4, n^2; y''=-y basis sin x, cos x, dim 2). Philosophically this is Apostol's default abstract setting, but no specific Apostol object carries these examples; no clean match.
Computational method (elimination) to extract a basis from spanning vectors via nonzero rows of R or pivot columns of A. Purely matrix/R^n algorithmic; Apostol has no such method in this block.
Independent columns <=> full column rank r = n. Rank is not present in this Apostol block (belongs to a rank/matrix topic). No counterpart.
Standard basis = columns of the identity (i,j,k). Apostol only mentions unit coordinate vectors in passing as an example inside a200; no dedicated standard-basis object to match.
